author: louis_231
quote:
How this game has a 94 critic rating and got a game of the year nomination is truly beyond me. Is this a bad game? Certainly not, but it has a lot of glaring issues that I'm surprised a lot of players haven't mentioned.

I'll start with the positives first - the soundtrack for this game is pretty good although I do think the Persona games have better soundtracks overall. There also seemed to be quite a lack of music and you end up hearing a lot of the same themes other and other again compared to other rpg's.

The story is also pretty decent and kept me hooked for a while. I do also like the more political nature of the game which I felt was done quite well. However some poorly written plot-twists and horrendous pacing (these characters never shut tf up) do hurt the story quite a lot and towards the end of the game I was struggling to really care about the narrative.

For the most part I also quite enjoyed the Archetype system. It isn't the most original in the world (it's just the job system from Final Fantasy V) but it gives you a lot of customisation in how you want to shape your party and offers a lot of freedom in how you approach the game. That said this system isn't perfect - a lot of the best Archetypes won't unlock until right at the end of the game and unless you were using a guide you will end up having to grind to level up Archetypes that you never wanted to use just so that you can unlock your characters best Archetypes which takes forevvveeerr.

Onto the stuff I didn't really enjoy - the dungeons are at best "ok" and at there worst, dull and repetitive. Every dungeon tries to have a gimmick to freshen things up but none of these gimmicks are particularly fun. One dungeon forces stealth mechanics whist another has a bunch of doors that will connect you to a random door on the other side of the map. Hardly fun and interesting stuff and a far cry from the dungeons in Persona 5.

Graphically the game is also very disappointing as well and looks like a PS3 game upscaled to 4K. Not the end of the world but they could have done much better. At least the anime cut-scenes and character portraits look nice.

The characters in the game are also quite a mixed bag. The main character is as bland as they come and has quite an annoying voice as well. The fairy companion Gallica is also fairly annoying (I never thoughtI would find myself missing Morgana). The rest of the cast are somewhat of a mixed bad - I really liked Heismay and Basillio but found Strohl, Hulkenburg and the other two to be quite uninteresting and I didn't really care that much about them. The main villain is great however although even he becomes more uninteresting as the story progresses.

Side-Quests were also quite a mixed bag. I really enjoyed the road trip aspect of doing Side-Quests and having to plan ahead and clear time from your calendar and prioritize runner activities - it felt like a fresh way to do Side-Quests, especially compared to the endless grind of mementos in Persona 5. That said towards the end of the game the Side-Quests felt very repetitive (especially the quest where you climb the same exact tower with the same exact enemies and then fight a re-skinned dragon boss 3 different times). You can't really skip the Side-Quests eitherunless you want to be severely under levelled.

Difficulty-wise this game was super easy apart from a random dragon boss 2/3rds through the game and then the final boss fight which just goes on for way too long. These fights were just incredibly difficult from nowhere unless you find a cheesey strategy on the Internet. The final fight also does not checkpoint before the final phase so if you die have fun replaying the same 30 minute section you just played. PS2 games had better design than this.

I really wanted to like this game as I love Persona 4 and 5 so much but I finished it just feeling bitterly disappointed and let down. I would recommend waiting for the price to go down or for the inevitable cash grab "Royal" version in a few years.

author: louis_231
quote:
Last of Us Part II may not have been the sequel we all wanted but does that inherently make it a bad game? Whether you enjoyed the story of the game or not Naughty Dog deserve tremendous credit for taking such huge risks in the plot of a triple A game in 2020 when they could have easily just copied the formula of the first game that they knew would work. When was the last time we saw a game take risks like this - Metal Gear Solid 2 maybe?

Not a lot of people are mentioning the gameplay of the game in their reviews and that is a real shame. Combat-wise this is probably the most satisfying third-person shooter I have played since the early Gears of War games and that is mostly down to how violent and satisfying it feels, when you shoot someone with a shotgun in this game you REALLY feel it. Overall the gameplay is very solid.

The game is by no means perfect however, it has some pacing issues and honestly could do with being at least 5 hours shorter. There are moments in the game when you are exploring for a while and it feels like the plot isn't really moving forward. The narrative structure of the game is also something I am not 100% keen on as it removes the emotion from some moments in the story that would have had more emotion to them if they were presented in a linear fashion. There are a few moments when the strange narrative structure works quite well however and it certainly makes the game feel unique and stand out.

We need more games to take risks like Last of Us 2 ore we will end up living in a generation of bland copy-paste sequels and I'm not ok with that.
